rows.evidence: 26 GPP NetCDF means cover 1859-1899 and 2259-2299 for 13 ESMs and explicitly identify GPP in kg m-2 y-1. Nine accompanying point shapefiles identify candidate dieback cells. Annual grids and tabular GPP support the calculation. First four records in each of 12 models verified that mean19th/mean23rd in filtered2-npp.xlsx equal corresponding GPP mean-grid values; matching numeric values occur in the _change.xlsx family.
rows.limitations: The nine shapefiles contain points with FID only, not polygon areas or a loss field. Sampling all 292 points against their paired GPP means found 292 future/past ratios below 0.30 but only 234 below 0.20; therefore they do not all satisfy the spreadsheet definition of over 80% decrease. The 24 summary tables have misleading npp filenames, require a coordinate/ID join, and _change IDs were one lower in the inspected pairs. Grids are global, not already clipped to the Amazon. Other periods, climate/NPP means, Koppen classes and regional summaries are separate outputs without matching dataset descriptions. Variable time bounds, inherited historical metadata, calendars and model-specific licensing still need validation before catalog publication.

No license or independent end-to-end reproduction was established; study code was inspected, not executed.

rows.evidence: The manifest lists ten BAU/GOV final scenario GeoTIFFs for border, carbon, fire, logging and MCWD. README_Fig5.txt explicitly identifies the Amazon degradation study; scenario and disturbance R scripts support its interpretation. The ten grids share a 900 m South America Albers grid (ESRI:102033).
rows.limitations: The rasters have no band descriptions or units and the scripts write differently named op/pe outputs, so the precise correspondence, units and 2019-2050 temporal meaning of each delivered final layer remain unverified. These are strong partial matches, not fully interpreted publication-ready assets. Script-referenced reference/carbon and other input paths are absent. Three supporting files are empty. Historical/coarse disturbance rasters are separate outputs; they are not silently equated to future scenarios. The leading space in the BAU logging filename is retained.
